slides.title: VMs with one Kubernetes control plane
slides.subtitle: OpenStack comparison / qrab target architecture
slides.notes: Five-minute presentation. The comparison uses the operator-supplied OpenStack topology and inspected qrab source, not an audit of the other cluster.

This is the operator-supplied topology in the other cluster. Services run in containers, but libvirt owns QEMU in host cgroups and OVN supplies guest networking. Do not infer a particular release, storage backend or floating-IP mode.

Kubernetes owns intent, manager owns the local QEMU process, and separate anchors give guest NICs independent Cilium identities. Node/storage helpers remain separately privileged. Image and volume scope is not yet a complete OpenStack product replacement.

slides.title: Where each VM boundary belongs
slides.subtitle: Engineering architecture review / code and ownership
slides.notes: Fifteen-minute technical narrative. Use the source register, capability ledger and detailed diagram catalog as the review appendix.

This is the operator-supplied topology in the other cluster. Services run in containers, but libvirt owns QEMU in host cgroups and OVN supplies guest networking. Do not infer a particular release, storage backend or floating-IP mode.

Kubernetes owns intent, manager owns the local QEMU process, and separate anchors give guest NICs independent Cilium identities. Node/storage helpers remain separately privileged. Image and volume scope is not yet a complete OpenStack product replacement.

slides.title: Remove services; assign the surviving work
slides.notes: These are responsibility mappings, not compatible APIs. Nova has more duties than issuing local hypervisor commands. Network address, routing and policy work survives removal of OVN. Image and volume requirements must be accepted explicitly.

slides.title: The code spine follows the ownership split
slides.notes: The workspace has 19 crates, 18 in the default path. Crate dependencies do not grant runtime authority: BMC/Redfish reuse manager abstractions while manager remains the private QMP owner.
Direct supervision aligns QEMU with its VM-specific container lifecycle and resource accounting. Process cleanup retains state authority through child reaping.

slides.title: A private QMP owner; a bounded public operation
points: Manager owns private QMP, QGA and VNC sessions.
BMC/Redfish authorize users before local control operations.
Protocol crates stay independent of Kubernetes, launchers, KVM and guest downloads.
slides.notes: The local socket trusts authorized same-UID peers. It is not another human login boundary or a generic remote QMP endpoint. Standalone embedded control is a separate deployment mode of the same abstraction.

A single Cilium fabric preserves separate management and NIC endpoint identities. The guest never shares the management network namespace. Each NIC costs a Pod/endpoint and requires explicit address/route ownership.

slides.title: One datapath still needs explicit control
points: Operator claims stable /32s and writes scoped FRR intent.
netd grants only authorized TAP/vhost descriptors.
Cilium policies enforce groups; labels alone do not create default deny.
slides.notes: Cilium BGP is a distinct upstream capability. Inspected qrab code uses frr-k8s. Ordinary attachment uses Cilium; duplicate-address live handoff depends on the local fork.

The target initiates the main connection, while bulk state moves source to target. Managers transfer supported VM state and switch control. Node peers transfer scoped conntrack. Shared disks are not copied. Guest-packet forwarding is another stream.

slides.title: A migration is an ownership transfer
points: Prepare a compatible target with empty identity state and fenced NICs.
Switch endpoint authority in the final pause; then adopt the exact target.
Refuse unsupported management state or auxiliary claims before unsafe side effects.
slides.notes: Powered-off VMs do not live-migrate, and the protocol is within qrab. Source completion, target adoption, forwarding grace and storage ownership must agree. No general cold-move/node-evacuation product is established.

slides.title: Three questions; three policy owners
rows: Kubernetes RBAC/admission or VM app roles
slides.notes: Kubernetes API authentication does not automatically authorize Redfish. A dashboard SVID is not a human console-admin grant. Guest workload identity and CHAP exports have additional distinct scopes.

The operator orchestrates scoped storage verbs through a separately authorized service. The root helper owns ZFS/LIO exports and fences. QEMU opens its own CHAP-authorized disk session; identity state uses another volume.

points: Assign every surviving OpenStack duty to an explicit owner.

slides.title: Operate the boundaries
slides.subtitle: Failure-first workshop / qrab and OpenStack
slides.notes: Twenty-minute workshop. Ask who owns the state, what fresh evidence exists, and what could still be active before proposing a repair.

This is the operator-supplied topology in the other cluster. Services run in containers, but libvirt owns QEMU in host cgroups and OVN supplies guest networking. Do not infer a particular release, storage backend or floating-IP mode.

slides.title: A symptom is not the owner
rows: Guest is off; console still reachable
Manager power state versus Pod lifecycle
Guest packets fail; VM probes pass
New disk operation fails; guest I/O works
Storage control API versus data connection
The finalizer that still owns cleanup
slides.notes: Existing QEMU, kernel queue FDs and disk sessions can have different lifetimes from their control services. Read the exact VM/Pod/anchor/export identities before acting.

slides.title: Scenario: the old node vanished
points: Identify the exact old VM/Pod UID and disk generation.
Keep unknown writer ownership visible.
Require clean release or a completed backend fence before replacement.
slides.notes: A node lease, NotReady condition, missing API object or forced deletion is not a storage fence. Hand-declared disks retain the documented explicit administrator recovery.

Use this diagram to separate storage API failure from iSCSI data-path failure. CHAP authorizes access but does not enforce one writer or encrypt the payload. Native transport encryption has its own verified segment.

Two VM Pods during a migration are not automatically split brain: the target is prepared/fenced and ownership must transfer through the protocol. Conversely, API object names alone do not prove a safe transfer.

slides.title: Scenario: the user logs in but cannot act
points: Distinguish valid human identity from VM action role.
Check exact service SVID admission independently.
Check API RBAC/admission only for the declarative API path.
slides.notes: Do not validate a user issue with an unrelated cluster-admin or service credential and call the original user path proven. The dashboard is a trusted ServiceAccount deputy.

slides.title: Deletion is not one operation
slides.notes: The audit tightened PVC and access-group provenance. Source now supports a seven-day root guest-disk reaper; that does not establish installed state or cover Released state PVs automatically.

slides.title: After a fix, prove the invariant
points: Power cycle: expected new child PIDs, same intended identity.
Migration: exact adopted target, stable NIC identities and no unintended active source.
Recovery: old writer cannot act; credentials/export generation are correct.
slides.notes: A successful API response alone does not prove guest application health, traffic continuity, disk consistency or cleanup completeness. Use the maintained focused checks for the actual affected path.

slides.title: Release and evidence boundaries
points: Source merge is separate from image publication.
Digest pin / identity enrollment is separate from rollout.
A dated live record describes its named versions and scope.
slides.notes: Do not automatically apply example VM bundles or recreate deleted test VMs. Operational notes and work evidence belong in qrab towl.

slides.title: Workload cutover checklist
points: Boot + firmware + identity + management access.
Data consistency + backup/restore + one-writer recovery.
Network policy/routes/DNS + observation + data-aware rollback.
slides.notes: The other OpenStack cluster must supply its actual workload/backend inventory. No transparent OpenStack-to-qrab live migration or universal feature parity is assumed.
